title: Weddings, festivals & occasions
goal: Wish people well for Eid, Ramadan, Nowruz, birthdays and weddings, answer their wishes, accept an invitation, and know what happens — and what to say — at a Pashtun wedding.
intro:
Pashtun life runs on occasions: two Eids, the month of fasting, engagements, henna nights, weddings that last for days, and — for younger people — birthdays with cake. Each has its own words, and getting them right is one of the warmest things you can do in Pashto.

You'll learn the set wishes (**اختر مو مبارک شه!**, **روژه مو قبوله شه!**, **خدای دې نېکمرغه کړي**) and how they're built, the right replies (**خير اوسې**, **ودې ګورې**), the vocabulary of a wedding from the **نکاح** to the **ډول** and the attan, and three ways to insist: **خامخا راشه** 'you must come', **پام کوه چې …** 'make sure …', **هېر يې نه کړې** 'don't forget it'.

grammar.title: Wishes and blessings: مبارک دې شه، خدای دې … کړي
grammar.body:
Unit 18 introduced **دې** + verb for 'may …'. Occasions are where you'll use wishes most, and there are two patterns.

**1. Congratulating: [occasion] + دې / مو + adjective + شه.** **شه** is the imperative of 'become', so اختر دې مبارک شه is literally 'your Eid — become blessed!'. Here **دې** and **مو** are the clitics 'your': **دې** to one friend, **مو** to a family, a group, or politely.
اختر **دې** مبارک شه (to a friend) · اختر **مو** مبارک شه (to everyone / polite) · واده مو مبارک شه · د زوکړې ورځ دې مبارک شه
An adjective agrees with the occasion: روژه (f) مو **قبوله** شه, but اختر (m) مو مبارک شه. (مبارک itself usually stays unchanged.)

**2. Blessings asking God: خدای دې + subjunctive.** Here **دې** is the wish particle 'may', and it never changes to مو: خدای دې عمر اوږد **کړي** 'may God give you a long life' · خدای دې نېکمرغه **کړي** 'may God make them happy' · خدای دې **وکړي** 'may God make it happen' — the reply when someone tells you their hopes.

**3. 'May it be …': … دې + وي**: کور دې ودان **وي** · ستاسو خوشالي دې تل **وي** 'may your happiness last forever'.

**4. The replies.** To any مبارک: **تا ته هم مبارک شه** (friend) / **تاسو ته هم مبارک شه**, or **خير اوسې** 'bless you'. When people congratulate *you* on a wedding or a baby, the classic reply is **ودې ګورې** 'may you see the same (one day)'.

examples.en: May your fast be accepted, brother.

examples.native: خدای دې عمر اوږد کړي، زويه.
examples.roman: xudā́y de ʿumr uẓd kṛi, zóya.
examples.en: May God give you a long life, son.
God willing — may God make it happen.

grammar.title: 'Be sure to …', 'make sure …', 'don't forget …'
grammar.body:
Invitations come with instructions, and Pashto has three handy ways to insist:

**خامخا** 'definitely, no matter what' + imperative — the warm, pushy 'you must': **خامخا** راشه! 'you have to come!' · خامخا له کورنۍ سره راشه 'be sure to come with your family'. A promise uses **حتماً** or **ضرور** + به: حتماً به راشم 'I'll definitely come'.

**پام کوه چې …** 'take care that …, make sure …' + subjunctive: پام کوه چې ناوخته **نه شې** 'make sure you're not late'. Polite / plural: **پام کوئ چې …**. On its own, **پام کوه!** or just **پام!** means 'careful!'.

**هېر يې نه کړې** 'don't forget it' — a negative subjunctive used as a gentle command. هېر agrees with the thing you mustn't forget: ډالۍ (f) **هېره** نه کړې 'don't forget the present', کارت (m) هېر نه کړې. With an action, add چې: **هېر نه کړې چې** انا ته زنګ **ووهې** 'don't forget to call Grandma'.

After چې, all of these take the ordinary **subjunctive** (perfective present) — the same form as after غواړم چې and بايد.

lines.en: I'll definitely be there. And make sure you save some Eid biscuits for me!

culture:
**Eid** lasts three days. People put on new clothes, men go to the Eid prayer, and the day is spent visiting — elders and relatives first — with three hugs and **اختر مو مبارک شه**. Every house sets out bowls of **کلچې**, sweets and dried fruit, and children collect **اختري** (Eid money) from every adult they meet. At **لوی اختر** families who can afford it sacrifice a sheep, goat or cow and share the meat with relatives and the poor. During **Ramadan**, people greet each other with **روژه مو قبوله شه**, and iftar invitations are a big part of social life. **Nowruz** (21 March) is the Afghan New Year, a public holiday with picnics and fairs; it is less marked in Pakistan.

**Weddings** are the biggest events of all and can stretch over several days: the engagement (کوژده, often with a شيريني خوري party), the **نکاح** with a mullah, the **henna night** (green clothes, the bride's hands hennaed, songs), and the main day, when the groom's **جنج** goes to bring the bride home to the sound of **ډول** and **سورنۍ**, and the men dance the **اتڼ**. Men and women usually celebrate separately — in Kabul and Peshawar this often means separate halls of a wedding hall. Guests bring money in an envelope or something for the new home; you don't need to bring anything big. Say **مبارک مو شه** to the family and **خدای دې نېکمرغه کړي** — and when it's your turn to be congratulated, answer **ودې ګورې**.

Birthdays are mostly a young, urban custom — cake, candles and a flood of WhatsApp messages. And whenever a friend has good news, expect the cry **شيريني!**

tip.title: Eid: what to say
tip.body:
- **اختر دې مبارک شه** to a friend, **اختر مو مبارک شه** to a family or politely.
- Reply: **تا ته هم مبارک شه** / **تاسو ته هم مبارک شه**.
- **کوچنی اختر** comes after Ramadan, **لوی اختر** is the Eid of sacrifice (**قرباني**).
- Children ask every adult: **اختري راکړه!**

tip.title: Wishes: … مو قبوله شه، خدای دې … کړي
tip.body:
- Congratulating: occasion + **دې/مو** + adjective + **شه**; the adjective agrees: روژه (f) مو **قبوله** شه.
- Asking God: **خدای دې** + subjunctive: خدای دې روژه قبوله **کړي**.
- 'May it be': … دې **وي**.
- Thank someone's wishes with **خير اوسې**.

lessons.title: Birthdays and good news

tip.title: Birthdays and treats
tip.body:
- **د زوکړې ورځ دې مبارک شه!** 'happy birthday', and add **خدای دې عمر اوږد کړي**.
- **لمانځل** 'to celebrate' is transitive: د زوکړې ورځ يې **ولمانځله** (ورځ is f).
- Good news? Friends will shout **شيريني!** — **شيريني راکړه!** 'treat us!'

tip.title: What to say at a wedding
tip.body:
- To the family: **واده مو مبارک شه!** and **خدای دې نېکمرغه کړي**.
- To a friend whose brother or sister is marrying: د ورور واده **دې** مبارک شه!
- When they thank you, they may say **ودې ګورې** 'may you see the same'.
- **ناوې** bride, **زوم** groom, **نکاح** the ceremony, **د خينې شپه** the henna night.

lessons.title: Invitations: be sure to come

tip.title: خامخا، پام کوه چې، هېر يې نه کړې
tip.body:
- **خامخا** + imperative: خامخا راشه 'you must come'.
- **پام کوه چې** + subjunctive: 'make sure …': پام کوه چې ناوخته **نه شې**.
- **هېر يې نه کړې** 'don't forget it'; هېر agrees with the thing: ډالۍ **هېره** نه کړې.
- Promise: **حتماً به راشم**.

new: خامخا راشه، ستا انتظار به کوو.
پام کوه چې ناوخته نه شې!

sentences.native: بله جمعه زموږ واده دی، خامخا راشئ!
sentences.roman: bə́la jumʿá zmuẓ wādə́ day, xāmaxā́ rā́shəy!
sentences.en: There's a wedding in our family next Friday — you must come!

sentences.native: پام کوه چې د واده کارت هېر نه کړې.
sentences.roman: pām kawa che də wādə́ kārt her na kṛe.
sentences.en: Make sure you don't forget the wedding card.

sentences.native: ډالۍ هېره نه کړې!
sentences.roman: ḍālə́y héra na kṛe!
sentences.en: Don't forget the present!

sentences.native: هېر نه کړې چې انا ته زنګ ووهې.
sentences.roman: her na kṛe che anā́ ta zang wə́wahe.
sentences.en: Don't forget to call Grandma.

sentences.native: ډول او سندرغاړی به هم وي.
sentences.roman: ḍol aw sandarġā́ṛay ba ham wi.
sentences.en: There'll be a drum and a singer too.

sentences.native: سندرغاړی ډېر ناوخته راغی!
sentences.roman: sandarġā́ṛay ḍer nāwáxta rā́ġay!
sentences.en: The singer turned up really late!

sentences.native: پام کوئ چې ماشومان ډول ته نږدې نه شي.
sentences.roman: pām kawə́y che māshumā́n ḍol ta nəẓdé na shi.
sentences.en: Make sure the children don't get too close to the drum.

sentences.native: خامخا له کورنۍ سره راشه.
sentences.roman: xāmaxā́ la kornə́y sara rā́sha.
sentences.en: Be sure to come with your family.

sentences.native: حتماً به راشم، ستړی مه شې.
sentences.roman: hatmán ba rā́shəm, stə́ṛay ma she.
sentences.en: I'll definitely come — thanks for asking.

sentences.native: پام کوه، په اتڼ کې ونه لوېږې!
sentences.roman: pām kawa, pə aṭáṇ ke wə́na lwéẓe!
sentences.en: Careful you don't fall over in the attan!
